subject: LuminaLabs connector validation & reference adapter runbook
messages:
From: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@luminalabs.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: LuminaLabs connector — initial compatibility pass

Hi Sergio / Karthik,

Thanks again for agreeing to validate the LuminaLabs connector with Redwood Private. We completed our internal adapter work and attached the connector spec (LL-connector-specs-v1.pdf). High level: the adapter exposes a gRPC front-end, supports mTLS, and expects model payloads in the proposed JSON-RPC shim (v0.9).

Asks:
- Can Redwood run a reference validation against a dedicated Private staging cluster next week?
- We’d like a checklist of technical tests you run so we can align expectations (auth, TLS, chunked responses, streaming, long prompt support).
- Any specific runtime constraints (sequence length, kv-cache expectations, quantization support) we should be aware of?

Proposed windows: Tue 2026-12-22 or Wed 2026-12-23 (PST). If those don’t work, we can push into early Jan.

Attach: LL-connector-specs-v1.pdf (spec, sample requests, test harness)

Cheers,
Emma Hayes
Partner Engineering Lead | LuminaLabs
emma.hayes@luminalabs.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

---
Note: internal stakeholders at LuminaLabs: Sean Park (integration lead).

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@luminalabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: LuminaLabs connector — initial compatibility pass

Emma — thanks for the spec and the clear ask. We’re happy to run the reference validation from our side. Quick notes and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Kickoff & scope
- We’ll run a compatibility matrix covering: connectivity (mTLS + SNI), auth flows (client cert + OAuth fallback), streaming/backpressure behavior, response size/fragmentation, and basic performance (p50/p95 token latency).
- Can you confirm whether the adapter supports token-prefetching / KV cache key exchange for decoder-only models? That changes how we validate caching behavior.

2) Staging window
- Our team can do Wed 2026-12-23 09:00–13:00 PST. Please confirm.

3) Access & artifacts we need from you before the run:
- Test credentials (mTLS cert + client key OR OAuth creds)
- A minimal corpus of sample requests (JSON) — the spec had examples but a few edge-cases help (long prompts, multi-turn prompts, function-call examples)
- Any rate-limits the adapter will enforce (RPS / burst) so we don’t trigger protections during validation.

I’ll draft a short runbook and post it to a shared Drive. Marissa, can you pick this up and add Redwood’s test checklist?

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

Adding a few tech items from the runtime team that will be part of validation. Short bullets so the test harness can be prepared: 

- Model formats: we will validate both FP16 and int8-quantized variants. Confirmed: adapter must be able to serve both without changing API surface.
- KV cache: we’ll check for a consistent cache key transfer. If your adapter does not support KV exchange we’ll fall back to full-prefix caching validation (expect higher latency in that case).
- Sequence length & attention: run tests at 1k, 2k, and 8k token prefixes (we can skip 8k if you don’t support it).
- Streaming: validate chunked-transfer encoding and partial token streams; confirm how you mark end-of-stream.
- Backpressure & retries: emulate load to exercise queueing (we’ll provide our harness).

If Lumina can provide the following by Monday EOD it’ll speed the run:
- mTLS cert + CA bundle or OAuth client creds
- A sample 2k-token test payload and an 8k tradeoff case (if supported)
- Expected behavior doc for streaming (end-of-stream marker, error semantics)

I’ll also drop a skeleton runbook into the Drive link Sergio mentioned.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@luminalabs.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Park <sean.park@luminalabs.ai>
Date: 2026-12-19T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: LuminaLabs connector — initial compatibility pass

Thanks — we confirmed the 2026-12-23 window and attached an initial run of the adapter against our local harness. Two quick notes from our end:

- Auth: the adapter supports mTLS, but the default installer also enables an API-key fallback that rejects requests over 1k RPS. We will provide a cert bundle and the installer config.
- Streaming: our implementation uses chunked JSON frames and a final sentinel {"done":true} to indicate completion.

Attached: manifest-test-results.csv (small-run results). The run shows failures in TLS negotiation when Redwood’s harness uses SNI with a SAN mismatch — we think there may be an SNI vs CN handling difference in the adapter's TLS stack.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood’s staging harness will use SNI (yes) and whether you can try a run that explicitly sets SNI to the CN to reproduce? Also — Sean will be on the call next week to help with TLS configuration.

Emma

Subject: Re: LuminaLabs connector — initial compatibility pass

> On Fri, Dec 18, 2026 at 12:20 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Adding a few tech items from the runtime team that will be part of validation. Short bullets so the test harness can be prepared:
> > - Model formats: we will validate both FP16 and int8-quantized variants. Confirmed: adapter must be able to serve both without changing API surface.
> > - KV cache: we’ll check for a consistent cache key transfer. If your adapter does not support KV exchange we’ll fall back to full-prefix caching validation (expect higher latency in that case).

Thanks Karthik — good clarity. We attached manifest-test-results.csv from our local smoke run. Summary of the failures:
- TLS: intermittent SAN/SNI mismatch under the harness (we saw a client hello with SNI set to the CN which our Go TLS stack rejected when the cert used alternate SAN ordering)
- Streaming: chunk boundary timing — occasionally the final sentinel is delayed and Redwood’s client-side timeout (default 3s) treats it as a failure. We can bump the sentinel timing but prefer to be explicit in the spec.

We’ll make two asks before the staging run:
1) Can Redwood’s harness set SNI to the adapter CN explicitly? (temporary workaround)
2) Can Redwood increase the streaming timeout to 6s for the test window so we can observe behavior under load?

We’ll upload updated installer config and the cert bundle to the Drive link.

— Emma

Attachments: manifest-test-results.csv (see rows 12-17 for TLS failure samples)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Emma Hayes <emma.hayes@luminalabs.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Park <sean.park@luminalabs.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: LuminaLabs — reference runbook and remediation plan

Emma / team — thanks for the early test artifacts and the manifest. We finished drafting a concise runbook and a short remediation plan for the two items you surfaced. I’ve attached redwood-runbook-lumina-20261220.md (run steps + expected outputs) and noted the changes below.

Summary (actionable):
- TLS / SNI: Redwood can run the harness with explicit SNI set to adapter CN. For the staging run we will set SNI to the CN as a temporary mitigation. Long-term recommendation for Lumina: accept both CN and SAN orderings in the TLS handshake (we included a small snippet in the runbook).
- Streaming timeout: We’ll run the staging window with an increased client-side streaming timeout of 6s. Our harness will log latency histograms for sentinel arrival; we’ll share those post-run.
- KV cache: If Lumina cannot support KV exchange, we’ll validate full-prefix cache behavior and capture the per-token latency delta (expect ~12–20% overhead).

Staging window confirmation: Wed 2026-12-23 09:00–13:00 PST. Please provide the cert bundle and installer config in the Drive folder before 2026-12-22 18:00 PST.

Next steps:
- Lumina: upload cert bundle + installer config + any additional test payloads (Emma / Sean)
- Redwood: run the test matrix, record p50/p95 token latency, collect streaming sentinel histograms, and share results in a follow-up summary within 48 hours of the run.

Links:
- Runbook (attached): redwood-runbook-lumina-20261220.md
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Lumina/connector-specs
- JIRA ticket: PARTNER-842 (we’ll use this for follow-up items)

If that all looks good, reply with a quick "ACK" and we’ll treat the staging window as confirmed.

Thanks — Sergio
